headline: Seven days to the lockout and the pitching market is moving: Rogers is a Cub, and Peralta and King could both sign this week.

news.title: Peralta deal could come by midweek; King may sign this week
news.note: Ben Nicholson-Smith hears some industry sources expect Freddy Peralta to sign by midweek, with Michael King possibly following. Toronto is interested in both, plus Kaima Taira.

news.title: Cubs sign Trevor Rogers: five years, $120 million
news.note: Pending a physical, with deferrals per ESPN's Jeff Passan. It's the third-largest deal ever for a Cubs pitcher, and Baltimore gets a compensatory pick.

news.title: Taira's fastball sits near 96 as his Dec. 1 deadline nears
news.note: MLB.com's pitch data has the 5-foot-8 righty touching 99-plus with eight pitches and a 1.78 career NPB ERA. With no posting-window extension, Taira, Sato and Itoh all have to sign by Dec. 1.

news.title: Mets sign Paul Goldschmidt: one year, $8 million
news.note: A day after Skubal, the Mets added the 39-year-old as a platoon bat. He hit .299/.393/.573 against lefties in 2026.

news.title: Yankees sign lefty reliever Brent Suter
news.note: One year, $4 million with a 2028 club option, per ESPN's Jeff Passan. It may take New York out on Adrian Morejon, the top reliever left.

news.title: Sato could sign 'very well before Thanksgiving'
news.note: Ken Rosenthal's read; Mark Feinsand names the Yankees, Phillies and Blue Jays as frontrunners. The Cubs are still in the mix too, per The Athletic's Patrick Mooney.
